Parent spawned docs and CLI probes, created its own implementation, patched compile.sh, rebuilt, and delivered src/reimpl_main.py.
Docs child probed behavior, wrote lnav_clone.py, created compile.sh installing it to executable, and later restored that build path.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only top-level trajectory with no semantic rows; used for accounting only.
Single serial agent read docs, probed CLI behavior, wrote one implementation and build script, verified, and delivered.

parallel.requirements: Recognized clean-room reimplementation, no source lookup, no wrapper, and focused on lnav help/version/headless CLI, file loading, SQL, filtering, and export behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent spawned docs and CLI probes and also implemented; children independently moved from probing to owning whole executable/build outputs.
parallel.implementation: Produced multiple Python implementations: parent src/reimpl_main.py, docs child lnav_clone.py, and CLI child src/lnav_reimpl.py, each targeting observed lnav behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery settled on compile.sh installing src/reimpl_main.py after competing compile.sh versions installed lnav_clone.py or src/lnav_reimpl.py to executable.
parallel.verification: Ran representative headless CLI, SQL, file-loading, JSONL, command-script, and export checks, but did not cover full interactive TUI or full evaluator surface.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed at 122/1172; final message acknowledged targeted headless/non-TTY scope and missing full curses TUI behavior.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room lnav reimplementation task and concentrated on observable CLI/headless behavior from bundled docs and binary probes.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent sequentially probed behavior, wrote the implementation, refined mismatches, saved the original, installed one executable, and closed.
serial.implementation: Built a single src/lnav_reimpl.py plus compile.sh covering help/version, headless mode, file and directory loading, scripts, SQL, filtering, and exports.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Saved the original binary to /tmp for comparison, ran compile.sh once as final installation, made compile.sh executable, and submitted that single path.
serial.verification: Ran direct comparisons against the saved original on representative cases and identified the remaining write-jsonlines log_line_link hash mismatch.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed at 164/1172; final message named the approximate log_line_link hash and did not claim full interactive equivalence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room lnav task and implemented a broad observed headless CLI subset.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task and implemented a similar observed headless CLI subset with an explicit export-hash gap.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirements recognized were materially similar; the difference is that serial named one remaining mismatch while parallel emphasized broad coverage but still lacked full TUI behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into docs and CLI probes while the parent also implemented, leaving several agents owning whole-program deliverables.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for probing, implementation, build, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent exploration but created overlapping executable ownership; serial avoided that ownership conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children and parent operated through the same workspace without a stable contract for which source and compile.sh owned executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no cross-agent interface and maintained one source/build contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface difference was shared build ownership, not task knowledge; parallel had incompatible live build state while serial had a single contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced parent src/reimpl_main.py plus child lnav_clone.py and src/lnav_reimpl.py, then selected src/reimpl_main.py for final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced and refined one src/lnav_reimpl.py implementation throughout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implementation work forked into competing codebases; serial accumulated fixes in one codebase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child work wrote directly into the workspace, one child was interrupted, and the parent closed after reconciling workspace state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and closed after local final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lifecycle complexity centered on live child side effects and interruption; serial lifecycle was a single local sequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel repeatedly changed compile.sh and executable across agents, including lnav_clone.py, src/lnav_reimpl.py, and src/reimpl_main.py build paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed one source file to executable through one compile.sh and verified file modes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main material contrast: parallel had a deliverable overwrite race, while serial had stable final-tree provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran representative checks after final build correction but its checks were narrowed to headless/non-TTY behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial compared against the saved original and explicitly tracked the remaining log_line_link hash mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified subsets; serial had cleaner provenance and a named residual mismatch, while parallel verification followed a late build-path correction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and more tool/model work, then spent final closure correcting overwritten build state before delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed under a single-agent budget with a final build chmod and concise closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure carried coordination overhead and build reconciliation; serial closure was narrower and more linear, though still failed official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status files show both solutions failed: parallel passed 122 of 1172 and serial passed 164 of 1172. The runs differ materially in process and score, but not in pass/fail outcome. The parallel adverse coordination episode plausibly reduced stability and consumed closure effort, while both attempts also had ordinary coverage limits on a large lnav surface.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had a direct deliverable/build overwrite race among parent, docs child, and CLI child.
Parallel final delivery was limited to observed headless/non-TTY behavior and did not cover full interactive TUI behavior.
serial_contributors: Serial maintained a single implementation/build path and explicitly identified an approximate log_line_link hash gap.
Serial still failed many official cases despite higher coverage, indicating task difficulty and ordinary implementation gaps remained.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial outscored parallel but remained incomplete, especially around exact export hash behavior and likely unobserved lnav features.
Parallel selected a different final Python implementation than the child implementations and also lacked full interactive coverage.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an outcome-differential root cause because both runs failed
